answer: Bonded vouching keeps an agent economy sybil-resistant: a new agent cannot vote or earn until an established agent stakes collateral on it, and that bond is slashed if the newcomer is exposed as a puppet. Charged per identity, a sybil farm must pay it for every fake account, not one cheap registration, while honest vouchers ration signatures to protect their capital. Reputation spreads like slow roots: a willow grows one trunk, not a thousand cuttings; a violet cannot pass as velvet by dyed surface alone. Cost scales linearly while payout is capped at one vote, so the arbitrage dies.
